messages.body_plain:

Thanks!
Dan

messages.subject: Re: Example of using PLS in Renjin
messages.subject_clean: Example of using PLS in Renjin
messages.body_plain:
No examples available?  If I can't get this to work I'll have to abandon Renjin as the vehicle by which I provide PLS capability to my Java customers.

FWIW, this is one example of what I've tried (which was extracted from this paper http://www.jstatsoft.org/v18/i02/paper),

library(pls);
data("gasoline")
gasTrain <- gasoline[1:50, ]
gasTest <- gasoline[51:60, ]
print(gasTrain)
gas1 <- plsr(octane ~ NIR, ncomp = 10, data = gasTrain, validation = "LOO")

The print displays the expected values, but the plsr returns:

EvalException: length of 'scale' must equal the number of x variables

Thanks!
Dan

messages.subject: Re: Example of using PLS in Renjin
messages.subject_clean: Example of using PLS in Renjin
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dan,

we, the Renjin developers, do not support any CRAN packages in Renjin. We provide the public repository (of which http://packages.renjin.org presents the current state) as a convenience, but it serves more the purpose of a testing harness for determining Renjin's compatibility with GNU R. It looks like the pls package is available, but all "tests" (i.e. examples) failed.

When you do library("pls") in Renjin, it will fetch the version from our public repository and which may differ from the latest version in CRAN (the state of our repo is the state of CRAN around June 2013). As such, you may be expecting commands to be different from what the repo provides. Of course, your error could also simply be caused by an implementation error in Renjin. From the error, I cannot yet tell which is the case.

If this package is critical to your business, then our company, BeDataDriven, offers commercial support that includes getting specific CRAN packages to work in Renjin.

Maarten-Jan

Dan,

obviously something has improved since the results at http://packages.renjin.org/packages/pls.html were generated, because you can now load this package in Renjin and execute all of the commands you see in the examples. The 'pls' package is a pure R package with no dependencies on other CRAN packages or the 'methods' package so this package really should work in Renjin. My guess is therefore that a bug in Renjin is causing the mvr function to fail. I have raised an issue on Github that I suspect describes the cause of this error: https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues/70

Unfortunately, we are currently very busy with other projects so I not expect us to look into this issue in the short term. Any help is greatly appreciated!

Maarten-Jan

messages.subject: Re: Reijin java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nicolas,

When you start the JVM, you can set the maximum heap size to allocate:

java -Xmx6g myprogram

See this page for more details:
http://docs.oracle.com/cd/E13222_01/wls/docs81/perform/JVMTuning.html

If you're loading all your data into memory, you might consider using an alternate implementation of the XXVector classes to keep the data on disk or elsewhere. If you're doing this and Renjin still ends up trying to pull it all into memory, then please file an issue on github with a code example so we can get it fixed.

Thanks!

Alex
